one_liner: Navy contracting officer who buys supplies and services for military family and morale programs in the DC region and supervises a small procurement team.
fit_summary: This job requires at least one year of hands-on contracting experience at the NF-03/GS-11/12 level: soliciting, negotiating, awarding and administering contracts, plus price/cost analysis and FAR/NAF knowledge, and likely an existing warrant path. Daniel's consulting work at IEM was on the government-client side of emergency management, and nothing on file shows contracting authority or supervising acquisition staff. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills are real assets but do not substitute for the specialized experience.
eligibility: Open to the public (NAF position), so no federal status or veterans' preference is needed.
One full year of specialized contracting experience equivalent to NF-03 or GS-11/12, in federal service or the commercial contracting sector.
Education: a bachelor's degree in any field, or 24 semester hours in business-related fields such as accounting, law, contracts, or economics. Confirm which you meet and have transcripts ready.
Security clearance is listed as 'Other'; expect a background investigation for a Navy installation role.
Must be able to act as an appointed Contracting Officer within warrant limits; supervisory duties make up 25% of the role.
strategy: Before applying, honestly inventory your IEM work. Did you write proposals, price bids, manage task orders, or work on FEMA/state contract deliverables? Only that kind of contracting-side work counts toward specialized experience.

If you supported proposals or pricing at IEM, describe it in contracting terms: RFP response, cost volumes, compliance with solicitation requirements, and the FAR clauses you worked with. List hours per week and dates for each job.
Show any team leadership briefly, such as leading project teams or mentoring staff, since the posting accepts 'project teams' as qualifying leadership.
Keep the resume to two pages, and mirror the five specialized-experience bullets in that order so HR can check each one quickly.
The window is short (Oct 30–Nov 7, 2026), so have your resume and transcripts ready before opening day.

More realistic: target GS-7/9 Contract Specialist (1102) trainee or Pathways roles, or FEMA/Virginia emergency-management and legislative-affairs posts. These build on Daniel's IEM and policy background.
resume_bullets: Prepared [number] proposal pricing/cost volumes in response to [federal/state] solicitations for emergency management services, ensuring compliance with [FAR/state procurement] requirements; [result, e.g., award value].

Managed contract deliverables and client communication for [contract type, e.g., firm fixed-price task order] with [agency], tracking [budget/schedule] and resolving [issue types] with government program officials.
Led a team of [number] staff on [project], assigning work, reviewing products, and coaching staff to meet [deadlines/quality standards].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you determined a price was fair and reasonable on a recent procurement.
How would you handle a purchase card request that looks like construction rather than supplies or services?
Describe a time you advised a program manager who wanted a procurement approach that conflicted with regulations.
How would you prioritize work and develop a small team of contract specialists and procurement technicians?
watch_outs: Daniel likely lacks the required year of hands-on contracting experience, and applying without it will result in an ineligible rating.
The application window is only nine days.
Patuxent River, MD is a long commute from Manassas. Telework is eligible, but the job is not remote, so confirm how often you would need to be on site.
NAF pay bands are separate from GS, and there is no promotion potential beyond this role.
